beats.care: A weaker rupee makes phones, laptops, fuel and studying abroad pricier. If you invest through SIPs, expect ups and downs; returns are never guaranteed.
beats.what: Foreign portfolio investors sold about ₹52,100 crore of Indian shares in October till the 18th, taking 2026's outflow to ₹3.12 lakh crore.
beats.why: Analysts say expensive oil, a strong dollar and higher returns on US government bonds are pulling global money away from India.

cards.note: Data from depository CDSL, as of 18 October.
cards.title: Money foreign funds took out of Indian shares

cards.body: When safe US government bonds pay more, big global funds can earn good returns without the risk of emerging markets. So some move money out of countries like India.
cards.title: why do us bonds matter to indian shares?

cards.body: It isn't all selling. Foreign funds turned small buyers on 16 October and are buying restaurant, healthcare and digital platform stocks while dumping banks and oil companies.
Foreign funds actually bought Indian shares in July and August. The flip to heavy selling came only in September.

cards.q: Will FPIs be net sellers for October overall?
How can foreign funds selling Indian shares affect you?
cards.why: Leaving funds convert rupees into dollars, and that extra demand for dollars can push the rupee down.

hook: Foreign funds pulled *₹3.12 lakh crore* out of India this year. Why leave?

learn.t: FPIs are foreign funds buying Indian shares. When they sell and leave, they swap rupees for dollars, which can weaken the rupee.

tldr: Foreign investors have pulled ₹3.12 lakh crore out of Indian shares in 2026, nearly double last year's outflow.
watch: Watch whether FPIs end October as net sellers. Analysts say crude oil prices and US bond yields will decide the mood.
